subject: BluePeak: unexpected 429s during nightly batch - mitigation plan
messages:
From: Marcus Chen <marcus.chen@bluepeak.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rate cap errors during nightly ingestion run

Alex —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s during our nightly ingestion window (~00:30–01:15 UTC) that impacted ~13% of jobs. The failures started around 2027-06-28 07:50 UTC and persisted intermittently for ~35 minutes before the pipeline retried successfully. Attached is a small log excerpt that contains token rejection traces and the client-side timestamps.

Impact: several downstream enrichment jobs timed out and one consumer backfilled. Not a total outage, but elevated error rates and retries that increased our compute costs.

Can you confirm whether this was a platform-side rate limit change or a tenant mapping issue? We need a short explanation and mitigation timeline so we can update stakeholders.

Attachment: bluepeak_error_log_0628.txt (log excerpt, 18KB)

Thanks,
Marcus Chen
Head of Integrations
BluePeak Inc.
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Chen <marcus.chen@bluepeak.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate cap errors during nightly ingestion run

Marcus —

Thanks for the log snippet and the quick heads-up. I’m sorry for the disruption. We’re triaging now and will provide a mitigation plan within the hour. Immediate notes:

- I’ve escalated to our runtime on-call (cc Monica).
- Can you confirm if the failing requests were all using the same API key / tenant id? That will help us determine whether this was a per-tenant mapping issue.
- If you prefer, we can temporarily raise the tenant rate limit while we investigate; that would require a short authorization from your side.

Short-term action I’m proposing (pending Monica confirm):
1) Temporary quota override for BluePeak for the next 6 hours to clear backlog.
2) Collect and correlate server-side KV-cache/quotas with your timestamps.
3) Deliver a root-cause note and a patch estimate within 48 hours.

I’ll follow up with concrete times.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: quick triage notes (do not forward)

Alex / Lauren —

Quick internal findings from the runtime logs (initial triage):

- We see a spike of quota checks where tenant_id=bp-001 was evaluated twice for the same token (duplicate mapping lookup) between 07:48:12–07:51:03 UTC.
- The quota lookup path hit an unexpected code branch introduced by our provisioning script in the 2027-06-15 deploy. That script added an extra mapping layer for multi-org tenants but did not set the override flag correctly, causing a logical double-count.
- Result: the effective token counter decreased faster than expected, triggering per-minute rate caps earlier than normal.

Immediate recommendation: create a temporary override that bypasses the duplicate mapping for bp-001 and roll the deploy fix to remove the extra mapping branch. I’ll prepare a patch and the override diff now.

Planned timeline (ETA):
- 09:55 PDT: push temporary override (6h window) — low-risk config change.
- 12:30 PDT: rollback the faulty mapping layer in staging and smoke test.
- 48h: patch release with unit tests and canary rollout.

Attachment: temp_quota_override_patch.diff

Let me know if you want me to apply the override now and if BluePeak will authorize the short window.

-Monica
Senior SRE, Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Chen <marcus.chen@bluepeak.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:57:00 -0700
Subject: Action: temporary quota override applied + next steps

Marcus / Alex —

Update from the runtime team: we have applied a temporary quota override for tenant bp-001 at 09:55 PDT. The override bypasses the extra mapping branch and restores expected token accounting. Early metrics show 429 rate dropped back to baseline within ~4 minutes.

What we did:
- Applied override (6-hour window) 
- Instrumented additional logging for the tenant path
- Opened INF-2348 to track the deploy fix and test coverage

Next steps & timeline:
- Today 12:30 PDT: deploy mapping rollback to staging and run smoke tests.
- Tomorrow EOD: begin canary rollout to production (1% → 10% → 100% over 48h) with automated rollback on error.
- Within 48 hours: full fix merged and scheduled release.

We will also create a short postmortem note and an itemized credit for the extra compute cost incurred by BluePeak due to retries.

Attachments: INF-2348 link (JIRA), temp_quota_override_patch.diff

Please reply if you’d like a 30-min post-incident review this week; otherwise I’ll send the postmortem and credit note when the fix is merged.

-Monica
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Chen <marcus.chen@bluepeak.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: BluePeak rate cap incident summary and credits

Marcus —

Thanks again for flagging this. Quick summary and ask:

Summary of what happened:
- Root cause: provisioning script added an extra tenant mapping layer without the override flag, causing duplicate quota evaluations and premature 429s for tenant bp-001.
- Mitigation: temporary quota override applied 2027-06-28 09:55 PDT; 429s returned to baseline within minutes. Full rollback to remove mapping layer validated in staging on 2027-06-28.
- Fix status: patch merged into main and scheduled for canary rollout (INF-2348).

Compensation and next steps:
- We will credit BluePeak for the additional retry compute costs incurred during the window (estimate being calculated; you will receive a cost breakdown by EOD tomorrow).
- Postmortem checklist attached: postmortem_checklist.pdf — this contains timeline, RCA, actions, and owners.
- We’d like to schedule a 30-min technical review this week to walk through INF-2348 and the mitigation testing; propose Thu 2027-07-01 10:00 PDT.

If that time works, I’ll send a calendar invite. Appreciate your patience — we’ll follow through until you’re satisfied.

Best regards,
Alex Martinez
